newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 1.00 to 2.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 1.00 to 2.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents lower Tuesday as traders expect the market to follow through on Monday's sell-off.

New York arabica futures tumbled yesterday as steep losses in the May contract ahead of its noon expiry dragged down the rest of the board. May plummeted 21.25 cents to end at 255.25 cents. Active July ended 6.90 cents lower at 246.25 cents after trading from 257.00 and 243.25 cents. The outer months finished down 1.00 to 6.35.
Focus this week is likely to be in London, where Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) is meeting to discuss its policy on export quotas in view of the recent explosive futures rally.

At a preparatory session of the ACPC six-member technical group on Monday, a draft proposal for a full session on Wednesday would have the group retain export quotas but include new flexibility on allocating them, delegates said.

At a producer/consumer meeting in London Tuesday, the head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers Federation, Jorge Cardenas, said he expected the coming October/September 1997/98 crop to be a normal crop of 12.2 million bags compared with 10.2 million bags in 1996/97.

International Coffee Organization (ICO), which is also holding meetings this week in London, said world coffee production could rise to 96.5 million bags in 1996/97 crop years from 86.2 million in 1995/96.
ICO also said world consumption was estimated at 74.7 million bags in calendar 1996, little changed from 74.9 million in 1995 and 75.3 million in 1994.
Stocks of green coffee in main importing nations, including reserves held in free ports, were estimated at 7.0 million bags in December 1996, the ICO said.

After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks continued to climb. Stocks increased by 5,510 bags, to 47,192 bags as of May 16. There were 4,000 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
London July robusta futures were broadly lower early Tuesday, in a correction to the market's recent run-up. LIFFE July was down $47 at the midday break, to $2,053.
